text: Zik looked at her.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then what are they telling us?
speaker: Zik

text: I don't know.
speaker: Ninsun

text: She lifted the compass instead. The needle swung from the courtyard to the black drop to the empty corridor and back again, circling once before settling—pointing straight down, through the floor, toward nothing any of them could name.
speaker: Narrator

text: The mark on Zik's palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate.
speaker: Narrator

text: He stepped toward the third door.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag caught his arm.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That one shows us gone.
speaker: Balag

text: I know.
speaker: Zik

text: The words of the man who had refused returned without invitation: That threshold does not ask. It only records the answer you already gave by arriving.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik set his foot on the threshold of the empty corridor.
speaker: Narrator

text: The floor held.
speaker: Narrator

text: He took another step.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind him the others waited. Enhedu watched with the flat attention of someone who no longer calculated odds the way she once had. Ninsun's stylus hovered over parchment that had nowhere useful left to write. Balag's grip on the axe was white-knuckled and certain.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik looked back once.
speaker: Narrator

text: Stay behind me.
speaker: Zik

text: He stepped fully through.
speaker: Narrator

text: The corridor beyond was the same corridor they had left. The same oily stone. The same slow drip of water that measured no hours anyone recognized. For three paces nothing changed.
speaker: Narrator

text: On the fourth the lesson was gone.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not the memory of his father.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not the sound of the old man's voice.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not the desert nights spent learning which stones would hold and which would open.
speaker: Narrator

text: Only the specific knowledge of how to test a floor—the exact sequence of weight and listening and the small adjustments of the ankle that had once been as automatic as breathing.
speaker: Narrator

text: He knew that something important had been taken. He could feel the absence the way he felt the mark under the linen. He knew it had once been the difference between walking and falling. The exact edges of the missing thing were already going soft, the way a word goes soft in the mouth right before it is lost entirely.
speaker: Narrator

text: His body still remembered.
speaker: Narrator

text: His hand still knew how to test the next stone. His feet still knew where not to fall. The lesson remained somewhere the City had not yet reached—buried in muscle and instinct too deep for the current extraction to dig out.
speaker: Narrator

text: For now.
speaker: Narrator

text: He stood in the corridor and waited for the others.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag came first, then Ninsun, then Enhedu. None of them spoke. The three doors behind them folded shut without a sound, as though the chamber had never held more than one choice to begin with.
speaker: Narrator

text: From somewhere ahead, deeper than the corridor they now occupied, three measured knocks answered the mark.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik kept walking.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind him Enhedu carried the gold she no longer wanted.
speaker: Narrator

text: Beside him Ninsun carried symbols that no longer yielded meaning.
speaker: Narrator

text: His body still knew which stones would hold.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik no longer knew what it was listening for.
speaker: Narrator
